+name: JavaScript-first example
+

+    paths: ['examples/javascript-first/**', 'scripts/run-javascript-first.sh', 'scripts/javascript-first.test.mjs', '.github/workflows/javascript-first-*.yml']

+

+  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
+  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: init.defaultBranch
+  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main

+  javascript-first:
+    # A relative call binds the gate to the same candidate commit as this caller.
+    uses: ./.github/workflows/javascript-first-gate.yml # zizmor: ignore[self-repository]
+    with:
+      source-sha: ${{ github.sha }}
+      javascript-command: node --test examples/javascript-first/native.test.mjs scripts/javascript-first.test.mjs
+      parity-command: node examples/javascript-first/check-parity.mjs
+      translation-command: node examples/javascript-first/generate.mjs --check
+
+  rust:
+    name: Test, build and package the translated example
+    needs: javascript-first
+    if: needs.javascript-first.result == 'success'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-rust
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ needs.javascript-first.outputs.tested-sha }}
+          persist-credentials: false
+      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@e2a55d2ffb04f378e9626c28d38b36d230d1e12f # input handling fix
+        with:
+          toolchain: stable
+      - name: Verify native Rust observations and package
+        run: |
+          test "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$TESTED_SHA"
+          bash scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh "$RUST_BUDGET_SECONDS" "Translated Rust checks" bash -e -o pipefail -c '
+            cargo test --manifest-path examples/javascript-first/Cargo.toml --locked
+            cargo build --manifest-path examples/javascript-first/Cargo.toml --locked
+            cargo package --manifest-path examples/javascript-first/Cargo.toml --locked
+            cargo publish --manifest-path examples/javascript-first/Cargo.toml --locked --dry-run
+          '
+        env:
+          TESTED_SHA: ${{ needs.javascript-first.outputs.tested-sha }}
+          RUST_BUDGET_SECONDS: 360
+
+  container:
+    name: Build translated container
+    needs: javascript-first
+    if: needs.javascript-first.result == 'success'
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 10
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-container
+      cancel-in-progress: true
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ needs.javascript-first.outputs.tested-sha }}
+          persist-credentials: false
+      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@v4
+      - uses: docker/build-push-action@v7
+        with:
+          context: examples/javascript-first
+          push: false
+
+  pipeline-status:
+    name: Pipeline Status
+    needs:
+      - javascript-first
+      - rust
+      - container
+    if: ${{ !cancelled() }}
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 5
+    steps:
+      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
+        with:
+          persist-credentials: false

+          HEAD_REF: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && format('refs/pull/{0}/head', github.event.pull_request.number) || github.ref }}
+        run: bash scripts/check-pipeline-status.sh

+name: JavaScript-first gate
+
+on:
+  workflow_call:
+    inputs:
+      source-sha:
+        description: Immutable forty-character commit SHA to validate, including release candidates
+        required: true
+        type: string
+      javascript-command:
+        description: Install dependencies and run the complete native JavaScript checks
+        required: true
+        type: string
+      parity-command:
+        description: Run the strict complete-feature parity inventory check
+        required: true
+        type: string
+      translation-command:
+        description: Regenerate from pinned source and reject target drift or carried code
+        required: true
+        type: string
+    outputs:
+      tested-sha:
+        description: Exact revision that passed all three prerequisite stages
+        value: ${{ jobs.javascript-first.outputs.tested-sha }}
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+env:
+  GIT_CONFIG_COUNT: '1'
+  GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0: init.defaultBranch
+  GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: main
+
+jobs:
+  javascript-first:
+    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
+    timeout-minutes: 30
+    concurrency:
+      group: check-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-javascript-prerequisite
+      cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}
+    outputs:
+      tested-sha: ${{ steps.revision.outputs.sha }}
+    steps:
+      - name: Validate requested revision
+        env:
+          EXPECTED_SHA: ${{ inputs.source-sha }}
+        run: '[[ "$EXPECTED_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-f]{40}$ ]]'
+      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
+        with:
+          ref: ${{ inputs.source-sha }}
+          persist-credentials: false
+      - name: Check exact checkout revision
+        env:
+          EXPECTED_SHA: ${{ inputs.source-sha }}
+        run: 'test "$(git rev-parse HEAD)" = "$EXPECTED_SHA"'
+      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
+        with:
+          node-version: '24'
+      - name: Native checks, strict parity and regeneration
+        id: revision
+        env:
+          EXPECTED_SHA: ${{ inputs.source-sha }}
+          JAVASCRIPT_COMMAND: ${{ inputs.javascript-command }}
+          PARITY_COMMAND: ${{ inputs.parity-command }}
+          TRANSLATION_COMMAND: ${{ inputs.translation-command }}
+          JAVASCRIPT_BUDGET_SECONDS: 1200
+        run: bash scripts/run-with-budget-warning.sh "$JAVASCRIPT_BUDGET_SECONDS" "JavaScript prerequisite" bash scripts/run-javascript-first.sh

+# JavaScript first and the single push gate
+
+For mixed Rust/JavaScript projects, implement and debug complete behavior in native
+JavaScript before compiling Rust. A browser UI, WASM wrapper, source envelope,
+matching filename set or equal test count does not establish behavioral parity.
+
+Maintain a feature inventory covering public APIs, CLI commands, errors, streams,
+persistence and deployment contracts. Record missing, partial and carried items;
+the production Rust gate must reject each. Use shared input/output fixtures and
+independent native execution, including refusal and boundary cases.
+
+Pin translation source and dependencies by immutable revision. Preserve typed meta IR (including Links
+Notation) intermediates, source hashes, target artifacts and refusal reasons.
+Regenerate into temporary output and compare tracked targets before Rust builds.
+A successful source round trip establishes preservation of source text; execution
+parity still requires observations from both native runtimes. Handwritten native
+adapters must be explicit inventory entries with their own tests.
+
+Use `.github/workflows/javascript-first-gate.yml` as a callable workflow. Supply
+real repository commands for the native JavaScript suite, strict readiness/parity
+inventory check and regenerate-and-diff check. The template deliberately supplies
+no default generator or placeholder successful command. Depend on its successful
+job with `needs:` before every Rust test/build/package/container/publish job;
+consume its `tested-sha` output as the checkout ref. A skipped gate is not success.
+For projects whose JavaScript port is unfinished, keep the readiness gate red and
+report the blockers rather than representing the rollout as complete. Adoption of
+this opt-in workflow does not by itself migrate this template's Rust-only sample.
+
+Avoid `workflow_run` when same-workflow `needs:` or reusable workflows suffice.
+If a separate workflow is required, check the source conclusion, repository/event
+trust, exact `head_sha` and artifact provenance; default `GITHUB_SHA` refers to the
+default branch rather than the initiating run. Keep untrusted PR execution read-only.
+
+Read-only CI checks may run in parallel after the JavaScript prerequisite. Give
+active releases, deploys, tag writes and generated-content pushes one shared
+repository writer group with `cancel-in-progress: false`; check cancellation must
+not interrupt publication. Reconcile current remote state before each write.
+
+Draft changes in bulk. Workers may inspect, edit and run bounded JavaScript checks,
+but exactly one coordinator owns git push. That coordinator stages a complete
+batch, verifies the exact candidate revision with required local checks, inspects
+the diff and pushes once. Wait for required same-revision CI before another push;
+combine all observed failures into the next batch. Push permission does not imply
+permission to merge, publish, deploy or clean user-owned caches.
+
+Bound expensive local work: avoid duplicate profile/target/feature configurations,
+share compatible build caches, limit compiler processes, measure wall time and disk,
+and stop when the agreed budget is exhausted. Never silently reduce production
+assertions, treat partial runs as green, or delete unrelated caches to regain space.
+
+References: [router issue 759](https://github.com/link-assistant/router/issues/759),
+[GitHub needs semantics](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/workflow-syntax#jobsjob_idneeds),
+[GitHub workflow_run](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/events-that-trigger-workflows#workflow_run),
+[Cargo build cache](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/build-cache.html).
+
+## Executable example and adoption
+
+`examples/javascript-first/` is a small, independent checked-i32-addition API.
+It includes native JavaScript, shared success/refusal/boundary fixtures, a typed
+JSON IR, a deterministic dependency-free translator and a strict inventory.
+SHA-256 hashes pin the native source, IR, fixtures and translator in `parity.json`.
+The translator refuses unsupported IR and unpinned inputs. The inventory names
+Rust's i32 input adapter explicitly; native invalid-input fixtures exercise that
+refusal while Rust tests observe the representable inputs and overflow cases.
+Compile-fail doctests also verify Rust rejects fractional and out-of-range input.
+This inventory covers this example's API only. Extend the inventory and fixtures
+to every feature of your actual application before adopting it for production.
+
+Run the prerequisite checks without installing Rust:
+
+```sh
+node --test examples/javascript-first/native.test.mjs scripts/javascript-first.test.mjs
+node examples/javascript-first/check-parity.mjs
+node examples/javascript-first/generate.mjs --check
+```
+
+The example caller is `.github/workflows/javascript-first-example.yml`. It runs
+these real commands through the reusable gate. Only success schedules the Rust
+job (tests, build, packaging and publish dry run) and the container build. Both
+check out `tested-sha`. The failure tests cover native failure/skip exit, absent
+commands, missing/partial/carried inventory entries, stale source hashes,
+generated drift and a mismatched revision, and check every downstream dependency.
+A workflow-level skipped gate also prevents those jobs through their explicit
+`needs` and success condition. No toolchain is installed in the prerequisite.
+
+For a release that generates a new candidate commit, pass its full SHA as the
+reusable gate's `source-sha` from the trusted candidate-generation job. Validate
+that candidate through this same gate before any compilation, package, container
+or publishing operation. The example uses its PR/push event revision. It does
+not accept arbitrary checkout revisions in a default-branch dispatch: untrusted
+code must execute in a context that cannot poison the default branch's caches.
+Actual publishing remains a separately authorized writer operation, serialized
+with other writers and bound to that tested candidate. The example only performs
+`cargo publish --dry-run`; it does not publish its demonstration package.
+
+When changing behavior, update native tests first, then native implementation,
+fixtures and IR. Review any newly required adapter or refusal. Update the pinned
+hashes only for reviewed source/translator changes, run the generator, and commit
+its output with the inventory. The gate requires a clean worktree after checking;
+commands must generate temporary artifacts outside tracked source or in ignored
+build directories. A caller cannot substitute a source round trip or placeholder
+command for executable native checks and complete feature parity.

+#!/usr/bin/env bash

+set -euo pipefail

+attempts="${DEPENDENCY_GRAPH_ATTEMPTS:-3}"
+delay="${DEPENDENCY_GRAPH_RETRY_DELAY_SECONDS:-2}"
+case "$attempts:$delay" in *[!0-9:]* | :* | *:) echo 'Invalid retry configuration' >&2; exit 2;; esac
+[ "$attempts" -gt 0 ] || exit 2
+state=unknown
+for ((attempt=1; attempt<=attempts; attempt++)); do
+  if response="$(gh api "repos/${REPO}/dependency-graph/compare/${base}...${head}" 2>&1)"; then
+    state=enabled
+    break
+  elif printf '%s' "$response" | grep -qiE 'rate.?limit|abuse|retry.after'; then
+    state=unknown
+  elif printf '%s' "$response" | grep -q '(HTTP 403)'; then
+    state=disabled
+    break
+  else
+    state=unknown
+  fi
+  echo "Dependency graph probe $attempt/$attempts was inconclusive: $response" >&2
+  if [ "$attempt" -lt "$attempts" ]; then sleep "$delay"; fi
+done

+[ "$state" != enabled ] || enabled=true
+if [ -n "${GITHUB_OUTPUT:-}" ]; then
+  printf 'state=%s\nenabled=%s\n' "$state" "$enabled" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
+fi

+    echo "::warning::$message Skipping Dependency Review for this pull request.";;

+use super::workflow_release::{job_block, release_workflow, step_block, workflow_job_names};
+use std::fs;
+
+/// Regression test for issue #100 (1):
+/// <https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/100>
+///
+/// `always()` runs a job even when the workflow run is cancelled, which is the exact
+/// opposite of what `!cancelled()` expresses. Combining them makes `!cancelled()` dead
+/// weight while reading as if cancellation still stopped the job. The terminal status
+/// observer also uses `!cancelled()`: it sees individual cancelled dependencies, but
+/// does not repaint a whole workflow run that a user or concurrency policy cancelled.
+
+#[test]
+fn release_workflow_never_combines_always_with_not_cancelled() {
+    let workflow = release_workflow();
+
+    assert_eq!(
+        workflow.matches("always() && !cancelled()").count(),
+        0,
+        "always() && !cancelled() is self-contradictory; use !cancelled() alone"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(
+        workflow.matches("always()").count(),
+        0,
+        "the terminal observer must not run after a whole-run cancellation"
+    );
+    assert!(job_block(&workflow, "pipeline-status").contains("if: ${{ !cancelled() }}"));
+    assert!(
+        workflow.contains("!cancelled()"),
+        "conditional jobs should still be guarded by !cancelled()"
+    );
+    // A bare leading `!` is a YAML tag indicator, so single-line guards must be wrapped
+    // in `${{ }}` (block scalars `if: |` are fine).
+    assert!(
+        !workflow.contains("if: !cancelled()"),
+        "single-line !cancelled() guards must be wrapped in ${{ }} to stay valid YAML"
+    );
+}

+fn pipeline_status_script_handles_all_conclusions() {
+    /// (case name, `NEEDS_JSON`, `IS_MAIN`, extra env, expected success)
+    type StatusCase<'a> = (&'a str, &'a str, &'a str, &'a [(&'a str, &'a str)], bool);
+    // Issue #156: a cancelled job on main is a hidden timeout only when this
+    // run was still the branch head; a superseded run's cancellation is churn.
+    let cases: [StatusCase; 6] = [
+        (
+            "success",
+            r#"{"test":{"result":"success"},"docs":{"result":"skipped"}}"#,
+            "true",
+            &[],
+            true,
+        ),
+        (
+            "failure",
+            r#"{"test":{"result":"failure"}}"#,
+            "false",
+            &[],
+            false,
+        ),
+        (
+            "cancelled on main",
+            r#"{"test":{"result":"cancelled"}}"#,
+            "true",
+            &[],
+            false,
+        ),
+        (
+            "cancelled off main without a proven supersede",
+            r#"{"test":{"result":"cancelled"}}"#,
+            "false",
+            &[],
+            false,
+        ),
+        (
+            "cancelled on main but superseded by a newer commit",
+            r#"{"test":{"result":"cancelled"}}"#,
+            "true",
+            &[
+                ("RUN_SHA", "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000"),
+                ("BRANCH_REF", "main"),
+                (
+                    "BRANCH_HEAD_SHA",
+                    "1111111111111111111111111111111111111111",
+                ),
+            ],
+            false,
+        ),
+        (
+            "cancelled on main while still the branch head",
+            r#"{"test":{"result":"cancelled"}}"#,
+            "true",
+            &[
+                ("RUN_SHA", "1111111111111111111111111111111111111111"),
+                ("BRANCH_REF", "main"),
+                (
+                    "BRANCH_HEAD_SHA",
+                    "1111111111111111111111111111111111111111",
+                ),
+            ],
+            false,
+        ),
+    ];
+
+    for (name, needs_json, is_main, extra_env, should_succeed) in cases {
+        let mut command = std::process::Command::new("bash");
+        command
+            .arg("scripts/check-pipeline-status.sh")
+            .current_dir(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR"))
+            .env("NEEDS_JSON", needs_json)
+            .env("IS_MAIN", is_main)
+            .env(
+                "GITHUB_REF",
+                if is_main == "true" {
+                    "refs/heads/main"
+                } else {
+                    "refs/pull/7/merge"
+                },
+            )
+            .env("WORKFLOW_FILE", ".github/workflows/release.yml")
+            .env_remove("RUN_SHA")
+            .env_remove("BRANCH_HEAD_SHA")
+            .env_remove("HEAD_REF");
+        for (key, value) in extra_env {
+            command.env(key, value);
+        }
+        let output = command.output().expect("run pipeline status script");
+
+        assert_eq!(
+            output.status.success(),
+            should_succeed,
+            "{name}: stdout={} stderr={}",
+            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stdout),
+            String::from_utf8_lossy(&output.stderr)
+        );
+    }
+}

+/// Regression test for issue #100 (2): the Dockerfile must be exercised at
+/// pull-request stage, not only after `cargo publish` inside the release jobs.
+#[test]
+fn release_workflow_builds_docker_image_on_pull_requests() {
+    let workflow = release_workflow();
+    let job = job_block(&workflow, "docker-build");
+
+    assert!(
+        job.contains("needs.detect-changes.outputs.any-code-changed == 'true'")
+            && !job.contains("github.event_name == 'pull_request'"),
+        "docker-build should validate code changes on PRs and main before release"
+    );
+    assert!(
+        job.contains("push: false"),
+        "docker-build must not push, so fork pull requests without registry credentials still work"
+    );
+    assert!(
+        job.contains("cache-from: type=gha"),
+        "docker-build should reuse the buildx layer cache"
+    );
+}

+/// Regression test for issue #154:
+/// <https://github.com/link-foundation/rust-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template/issues/154>
+///
+/// Unscoped `type=gha` cache entries all land in the default `buildkit` scope,
+/// so the pull-request image build and each docker-publish matrix leg evict and
+/// overwrite each other's exported layers. Every GHA cache reference must pin an
+/// explicit scope.
+#[test]
+fn release_workflow_scopes_every_gha_buildx_cache() {
+    let workflow = release_workflow();
+
+    for line in workflow.lines().filter(|line| {
+        line.trim_start().starts_with("cache-from: type=gha")
+            || line.trim_start().starts_with("cache-to: type=gha")
+    }) {
+        assert!(
+            line.contains("scope="),
+            "GHA buildx cache reference lacks an explicit scope, so it shares \
+             the default 'buildkit' scope with unrelated builds:\n{line}"
+        );
+    }
+
+    let docker_build = job_block(&workflow, "docker-build");
+    assert!(
+        docker_build.contains("cache-from: type=gha,scope=docker-image")
+            && docker_build.contains("cache-to: type=gha,mode=max,scope=docker-image"),
+        "the pull-request image build should use a dedicated scope"
+    );
+
+    let docker_publish = job_block(&workflow, "docker-publish");
+    assert!(
+        docker_publish.contains("cache-from: type=gha,scope=${{ matrix.platform }}")
+            && docker_publish.contains("cache-to: type=gha,mode=max,scope=${{ matrix.platform }}"),
+        "each docker-publish matrix leg should scope its cache by platform so \
+         the legs do not overwrite each other"
+    );
+}

+/// Regression test for issue #100 (3): a pull request that is green in isolation can
+/// still break `main` (semantic merge conflict), and committed credentials must be flagged.
+#[test]
+fn release_workflow_simulates_fresh_merge_and_scans_for_secrets() {
+    let workflow = release_workflow();
+
+    assert!(
+        job_block(&workflow, "fresh-merge").contains("bash scripts/simulate-fresh-merge.sh"),
+        "fresh-merge job should run the merge simulation script"
+    );
+    assert!(
+        job_block(&workflow, "secrets-scan").contains("secretlint"),
+        "secrets-scan job should run secretlint"
+    );
+
+    let script = fs::read_to_string(format!(
+        "{}/scripts/simulate-fresh-merge.sh",
+        env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")
+    ))
+    .unwrap();
+    assert!(
+        script.contains("set -euo pipefail"),
+        "merge simulation should fail fast on unexpected errors"
+    );
+    assert!(
+        script.contains("git merge --no-edit"),
+        "merge simulation should actually merge the head into the base tip"
+    );
+
+    assert!(
+        std::path::Path::new(&format!(
+            "{}/.secretlintrc.json",
+            env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")
+        ))
+        .exists(),
+        "secretlint requires a .secretlintrc config file to run"
+    );
+}

+    );

+#[test]
+fn rustdoc_warnings_are_gated_before_release_jobs() {
+    let workflow = release_workflow();
+
+    // The first `cargo doc` invocation must be the pre-release lint gate, not
+    // the post-build deploy-docs job. See issue #96.
+    let first_doc_build = workflow
+        .find("cargo doc")
+        .expect("release workflow should build documentation");
+    for release_job in ["auto-release", "manual-release", "deploy-docs"] {
+        let job_start = workflow
+            .find(&format!("  {release_job}:\n"))
+            .unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("missing job {release_job}"));
+        assert!(
+            first_doc_build < job_start,
+            "first `cargo doc` must run before the {release_job} job"
+        );
+    }
+
+    let lint = job_block(&workflow, "lint");
+    let lint_docs = step_block(lint, "Build documentation");
+    assert!(lint_docs.contains("RUSTDOCFLAGS: -D warnings"));
+    assert!(lint_docs.contains("cargo doc --no-deps --all-features"));
+}
